title: Ephemeral GPU pool hopscotch - incident breadcrumbs
content:
Quick summary:
- Observed repeated capacity churn (nodes coming up, then drained/removed within ~3–7 minutes) across the dedicated GPU pool during three short bursts on 2025-02-18/19. Pattern looked like a hopscotch: scale-up -> pods scheduled -> pods sit in Init/CrashLoop or warm slow-start -> autoscaler scales another node -> older nodes drained -> ultimate capacity stays below desired for ~10–18 minutes.

Why I’m writing this: personal breadcrumbs while debugging interaction between our dedicated autoscaler, model warm-up logic, and node lifecycle hooks. I want an easy timeline + commands so we can reproduce and test mitigation ideas.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-18 02:03 UTC — first complaint: increased 429s reported from internal canary test.
- 02:07 UTC — autoscaler reacts, scales pool from 6->9 GPUs.
- 02:09–02:12 UTC — several pods stuck in Init (image pull + model fetch) or OOM/killed during python process startup.
- 02:11 UTC — autoscaler considers nodes underutilized and starts scale-down (racey).
- 02:15 UTC — new nodes get preempted/drained; end-to-end latency remains high for ~12 minutes.

Evidence/log snippets: (copied raw during incident)
- kubectl describe pod serving-abc-xyz -n dedicated-prod:
  Init Containers:
  "Waiting: CrashLoopBackOff: back-off 5m0s"
  Events:
  "Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up sandbox containerd: failed to run prestart hook: error executing hook: exit status 1"

- autoscaler logs excerpt (internal autoscaler):
  "2025-02-18T02:08:44Z INFO scaling to 9 (capacity shortfall 3)
   2025-02-18T02:10:34Z WARN node/node-47 idle for 2m, marking candidate for drain
   2025-02-18T02:11:12Z INFO scale down decision: nodes_to_remove=[node-47] reason=underutilized
   2025-02-18T02:11:15Z INFO scale up in progress: requested 2 more GPUs"

- kubelet logs around pod startup (node-52):
  "Feb 18 02:09:40 kubelet[1234]: Pulling image...
   Feb 18 02:09:58 kubelet[1234]: Started container model-server
   Feb 18 02:10:05 model-server[pid]: loading weights, ETA ~60s
   Feb 18 02:10:23 model-server[pid]: allocation failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
   Feb 18 02:10:23 kernel: Out-of-memory: Kill process 5423 (python)"

Commands I ran while poking (and outputs):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-prod -o wide
  "RESTARTS   AGE
   serving-abc-xyz   4   7m
   serving-def-123   0   90s"

- kubectl top node | grep gpu
  "node-51  gpu: 0/1
   node-52  gpu: 0/1
   node-53  gpu: 0/1"
  Note: metrics delayed; top shows 0 because model server not fully initialized and not reporting GPU metrics until after CUDA context created.

- gcloud compute instances describe node-52 --format='value(status, tags)'
  "RUNNING  [dedicated-gpu, preemptible]"

- checked model fetch times via s3 logs: average model download ~22s (with P95 40s) for this model artifact.

Initial hypotheses (unordered):
1) Cold-start warmup + model download latency leads to pods occupying new nodes without actually serving tokens for ~20–60s. Autoscaler uses pod CPU/GPU metrics or scheduling heuristics that incorrectly mark nodes as underutilized and schedules scale-downs too aggressively.
2) Our warm-start readiness probe is too optimistic — it marks pod ready before CUDA allocation completes, so traffic routes to pod while it still OOMs or slow-starts.
3) Node labeling + preemptible instances: we use preemptible-backed nodes in this pool for burst capacity. Short-lived preemptions + pod evictions create cascade as autoscaler keeps topping up but pods keep failing to warm.
4) Model server memory footprint varies with batch size and quantized model; if autoscaler scales nodes but scheduler places multiple heavy pods on one node before prior pods warmed, GPU memory contention causes OOM.
5) Leader election race in the autoscaler controller triggers a temporary mis-evaluation of capacity (suspect related to transient etcd latency during ~02:10 UTC window).

Things I tried (actions & temporary mitigations):
- Increased minPoolSize for the dedicated pool from 4 to 6 for the next hour to reduce immediate churn — reduced 429s but increased cost. (Command: api call to infra:PATCH /pools/dedicated-gpu {min=6})
- Added a preStart sleep (20s) in model-server container to make image pull/cache + model download more likely to finish before readiness probe toggles. This lowered CrashLoop frequency but is a hack.
- Changed readiness probe to check for /healthz?ready_model=true (requires model-server to explicitly report CUDA allocated) — still needs instrumenting in model binary.
- Disabled scale-down in autoscaler temporarily: set cooldown window to 10m from 2m. Observed fewer churn cycles in the next burst.

Repro steps (mini):
1) Simulate traffic spike via internal bench: bench-client --qps 150 --duration 30s -> triggers scale up.
2) Deploy model that has large cold model fetch (~>25s) and memory footprint (non-quantized).
3) Observe autoscaler growth, then set simulated node preemption after 3–5 minutes (kill node) to see reactivity.

Immediate theories to validate (next experiments):
- Validate metrics used by autoscaler: is it checking GPU-util or pod-reported metrics? Grab autoscaler config (scalingPolicy) and confirm metric window (we suspect 30s window is too short).
- Instrument model-server to call a /ready endpoint only after CUDA context + model mmap is done. Compare latency/429 before/after.
- Swap preemptible nodes to non-preemptible for one hour and re-run bench to see if preemption is the amplification factor.
- Try node reservation: make autoscaler aware of warm-up time by adding a "warmup_grace_seconds" to avoid scaling down nodes that have pods in Init for < 120s.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns autoscaler config? (I think infra-team + serving-runtime). Need owner to review: Diego Ramirez (cc-ed).
- What is current TTL for image/model cache on nodes? If we can keep model cached, warm starts get faster.
- Can we add a cheap CUDA context-only sidecar that initializes GPU memory earlier and exits, marking node as warmed? (weird but possibly effective)
- Should we prefer non-preemptible nodes for the small tail of capacity when latency SLOs are at risk?

Notes-to-self (observational):
- Observed pattern looks different from simple autoscaler flapping: it's a timing mismatch. New node created -> pods scheduled -> heavy IO (model download) + warm memory alloc -> autoscaler thinks node idle (based on immediate CPU/GPU metrics) and removes it -> remaining pods get spilled to other nodes -> cascade.
- The preStart sleep hack lowered events but is not acceptable long-term. We need a readiness-based fix.

Quick action plan (short term):
- 1) Instrument model-server ready probe to include CUDA context allocation (assign to me + Chen Li).
- 2) Bump autoscaler scale-down cooldown to 10m for dedicated pool until we have readiness fix (Diego to apply via infra ticket).
- 3) Run controlled bench against non-preemptible nodes for 3 hours to isolate preemption effect (owner: infra).
- 4) Draft a small PR to add a warmup_grace_seconds parameter to autoscaler and run A/B test (owner: me).

Longer term ideas (notes):
- Move models to a lightweight cache tier / prefetch mechanism during low-traffic windows.
- Expose a "model hotness" metric to autoscaler so it can prioritize nodes with cached artifacts.
- Consider allowing our runtime to request a tiny reserved GPU allocation for warm-up before receiving traffic (this prevents immediate memory OOM during initial batch).

If you read this and have ideas, ping me in #eng-runtime or drop a note here. Will update this doc as I test the readiness probe change.

-- Ava
